summary: The crew eat breakfast, a substance between yogurt and cellulite, and joke about what it reminds them of. Dozer explains it is a single-celled protein with synthetic aminos, vitamins, and minerals grown in a vat. Mouse brags that he wrote the Agent training program Neo ran through, then offers to arrange a meeting with a woman in a red dress he designed, prompting Switch to call him a digital pimp. Morpheus enters, orders everyone onto twelve-hour standby, and announces he is taking Neo to see the Oracle before leaving.

what_changes.before: A newcomer being fed and questioned about the ship's food and his training
what_changes.after: Learns he is about to be taken to see the Oracle
what_changes.evidence: MORPHEUS: I'm taking Neo to see her. ... NEO: See who? TANK: The Oracle.

what_changes.before: An ordinary crew member at breakfast
what_changes.after: Reveals himself as the author of the Agent training program and its designer of a woman, then pitches Neo a private meeting
what_changes.evidence: MOUSE: So I understand you've run through the Agent training program? You know, I wrote that program. ... The woman in the red dress. I designed her.

what_changes.before: Absent while the crew relax at a meal
what_changes.after: Takes charge and claims Neo for a mission to the Oracle
what_changes.evidence: MORPHEUS: I want everyone on twelve-hour standby. We're going in. I'm taking Neo to see her.

event_hint.one_line: The crew share a meal and banter before Morpheus interrupts to take Neo to the Oracle.

minds.wants: To be seen by the newcomer as the ship's most clever, dangerous mind — author of the training program and, more tellingly, designer of the woman inside it.
minds.feels: A mix of pride and hunger. In a world of grey vat-goop, he has made something private and pleasurable, and he wants that creation to buy him status and a private audience with Neo.
minds.shows: Boastful, sidling, conspiratorial — the 'digital pimp' who frames selling a fantasy as philosophy ('To deny our impulses is to deny the very thing that makes us human').
minds.basis: He brags 'I wrote that program,' then 'The woman in the red dress. I designed her,' sidles up and offers 'a more personalized milieu,' and defends himself with a grand statement about human impulses.

believes_about.belief: That Neo will be impressed and grateful for a private encounter with his creation.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo is on his way to the Oracle; Mouse's pitch is small change to him and is about to be cut off entirely by Morpheus.

believes_about.belief: That her 'digital pimp' jab is puritanical hypocrisy he can lecture away.
believes_about.wrong_because: Switch is reading his neediness, not his philosophy; her contempt is for the performance, not the impulse.

minds.wants: To puncture Mouse's self-importance and keep the hierarchy honest in front of the newcomer.
minds.feels: Amused but unimpressed — she has heard this routine before and finds it tiresome rather than impressive.
minds.shows: Dry, surgical one-liners: 'technically neither did you' and 'The digital pimp hard at work,' delivered without raising her voice.
minds.basis: She undercuts Mouse's Cream of Wheat logic with a technicality and labels his offer to Neo with a withering epithet.

believes_about.belief: That his bragging is transparent need for attention, not genuine cleverness worth indulging.
believes_about.wrong_because: He actually did write the program and design the woman, so the boast is true — she is dismissing the manner, not the fact.

minds.wants: To take his place among this crew and understand the world he has entered.
minds.feels: A newcomer's tentative ease — he is being fed, teased, and included, and for a moment the horror of the real (see sc-073) recedes into ordinary crew banter.
minds.shows: He eats the goop, plays along, and asks the plain question 'See who?' when Morpheus names an unknown person.
minds.basis: He accepts Tank's 'breakfast of champions,' listens to Mouse, and is visibly uninformed about the Oracle.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus's certainty about him is settled and singular.
believes_about.wrong_because: From sc-073 he has just learned Morpheus believed the same about five others, all dead — a doubt he will raise in ev-021 that this scene's announcement reignites.

minds.wants: To move the ship from respite to the decisive step of his project: bringing Neo to the Oracle.
minds.feels: Focused urgency — the prophecy he has staked everything on (and that Cypher in sc-073 called a 'mindjob') is about to be tested, and he will not let breakfast chatter delay it.
minds.shows: No greeting, no explanation — a command ('twelve-hour standby. We're going in.') and a claim of ownership ('I'm taking Neo'), then he leaves before questions form.
minds.basis: He enters, issues standing orders, and singles out Neo with 'I'm taking Neo to see her,' exiting immediately.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is ready to be taken to the Oracle and will accept the journey on faith.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo is still asking 'See who?' and carries fresh doubts from Cypher about five dead predecessors — he is being led, not yet a believer.

minds.wants: To ground the crew's nonsense in fact and give the newcomer an honest answer about what he is eating.
minds.feels: Contented, matter-of-fact — he enjoys being the one who actually knows how the ship works.
minds.shows: A calm technical correction of Mouse's absurdity: 'single-celled protein... grown in a vat.'
minds.basis: He authoritatively explains the substance's composition after the others joke about its taste.

believes_about.belief: That a straight scientific answer will end Mouse's game.
believes_about.wrong_because: Mouse immediately pivots past it ('Oh no, it doesn't have everything the body needs') to resume his pitch, so the correction only briefly checks him.

minds.wants: To enjoy the ritual of the meal and the running joke at Mouse's expense.
minds.feels: Relaxed and superior — he knows Mouse's moves and narrates them for the table.
minds.shows: Wry additions to the goop gag ('breakfast, lunch, and dinner of champions') and a knowing 'Here it comes' when Mouse starts his pitch.
minds.basis: He riffs on Tank's line and telegraphs Mouse's approach before the woman-in-red offer lands.

believes_about.belief: That Mouse's woman-in-red pitch is a tired, predictable routine the whole crew has seen.
believes_about.wrong_because: He treats it as pure comedy, missing that Mouse is genuinely using it to court status and a private connection with Neo.

minds.wants: To welcome Neo and set a warm, ordinary tone for his first shared meal with the crew.
minds.feels: Genial and protective — he is the one making sure the newcomer is fed and included.
minds.shows: A beaming 'Breakfast of champions' as he slides the bowl over and sits with the others.
minds.basis: He serves Neo first and opens the meal with a friendly, teasing line.

believes_about.belief: That Neo will relax into crew life now that the hard training and revelations are momentarily behind him.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus is about to pull Neo straight into the Oracle mission, so this respite is over almost as soon as Tank offers it.

connects_back: sc-073: Neo's conversation with Cypher seeded doubt about Morpheus's prophecy (five dead Ones), which this scene's Oracle announcement reawakens beneath Neo's calm.
sc-074: Cypher's betrayal and deal with Agent Smith are already in motion, so this convivial crew meal is being watched by a man who has just sold them out.
The ship's austere reality (vat-grown food, standby duty) continues the world-building of scarcity established across the earlier ship scenes.
sets_up: ev-021: Morpheus taking Neo 'to see her' launches the journey to the Oracle and its prophecy.
ev-019/ev-020: The crew's relaxed rapport and Mouse's self-promotion establish the bonds and status that Mouse's death in ev-022 will rupture.
ev-023: Morpheus's 'twelve-hour standby, we're going in' order puts the crew on alert for the mission that leads to Cypher's betrayal aboard the ship.
dramatic_function: A deliberate calm before the storm: it humanizes the crew and normalizes Neo's place among them so the coming betrayals and deaths land with weight, while Morpheus's abrupt interruption pivots the story from initiation to the Oracle test.
